negative_findings.description: No dedicated 'Javne nabavke' or 'Plan javnih nabavki' page was found on cbcg.me. A direct fetch of the /me/javnost-rada section index returned the full subsection tree (Aktuelno, Izlaganja, Blog, Multimedija, Tenderi i oglasi, Informacije, Elektronski servisi) with no procurement-plan, contracts-register or award-notice subsection.
negative_findings.result_summary: Procurement plan is not proactively published on the CBCG website under a discoverable path; only ad-hoc 'Tenderi i oglasi' items exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The annual procurement plan is the single best forward-looking artefact for this cell. Its absence means the pipeline must be reconstructed from CEJN, the Strategic Plan, IFI procurement plans, and FOI requests — and yet Montenegrin media (borba.me, dan.co.me) clearly report on CBCG plan line items, so a plan document does exist and circulates somewhere.

negative_findings.description: https://cejn.gov.me/tenders returned essentially an empty shell (only the token 'CeJN') on a plain HTTP fetch, so no listing, filter model, URL pattern or registration requirement could be observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: National e-procurement portal content is not reachable without JavaScript rendering.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CEJN is the statutory home for CBCG's domestically-run procedures. Until a headless-browser or API path is established, the entire national-portal leg of this cell is uncollectable, and CBCG award notices there would be missed.

negative_findings.description: https://www.cbcg.me/e/javnost-rada/tenderi-i-oglasi returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch even though the URL is indexed by search engines and the parallel /me/ locale path served full content.
negative_findings.result_summary: English locale of the CBCG tender page could not be retrieved on this attempt; hypothesis is locale routing or bot handling, not removal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the collector is pointed only at the English locale it will silently collect nothing. Collection should default to the /me/ locale with the English one as a secondary.

negative_findings.description: A targeted TED search for a Central Bank of Montenegro cash-processing notice returned only ECB tenders and unrelated Montenegro notices; the CBCG cash-equipment procurement was found instead via Montenegrin news reporting the EU Funding & Tenders Portal references EC-ENEST/TGD/2026/EA-LOP/0101 and EC-ENEST/TGD/2026/EA-LOP/0005.
negative_findings.result_summary: The notice is real and well-referenced, but it was not locatable through a generic TED keyword search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword search over TED is not a sufficient collection strategy for this cell. Collection must query the Funding & Tenders Portal by programme (EC-ENEST) and country, and must key on reference-number families, because the buyer name shown may be the Ministry of Finance rather than CBCG.

negative_findings.description: Search noise: 'Centralna banka Crne Gore' collides heavily with commercial banks carrying similar names (Prva banka Crne Gore, Prva Banka Crne Gore) and with Serbia's portal 'jnportal.ujn.gov.rs', which is a different country's system despite the near-identical acronym UJN.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several searches returned Serbian portal and commercial-bank results as top hits.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collectors must pin on the exact buyer string plus a ME country/domain constraint, or they will ingest Serbian procurement and commercial-bank content as CBCG signal.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language notice was found using RTGS/RTS/X-specific procurement vocabulary ('nabavka platnog sistema', 'nadogradnja RTGS'). RTS/X coverage was found only as programme/description pages, never as a tender document.
negative_findings.result_summary: The RTS/X procurement itself (2005-generation system replaced in 2025) has no publicly discoverable notice in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single largest payment-infrastructure purchase CBCG has made in twenty years may have been procured via a route that is not publicly indexed (direct arrangement with a central-bank service provider, IFI-financed, or exempt). Establishing how RTS/X was procured is the key to predicting how the next one will be.

coverage_gaps.description: CEJN (cejn.gov.me) could not be read without JavaScript, so CBCG's national-portal procurement record — plans, tender documentation, award-outcome notices — remains unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a headless-browser session against cejn.gov.me/tenders, filter naručilac = 'Centralna banka Crne Gore', and capture the XHR/JSON endpoints the SPA calls so collection can poll JSON directly. Also test whether an anonymous account unlocks fuller search.

coverage_gaps.description: CBCG's annual procurement plan (plan javnih nabavki) and any contract register were not located in any public location.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: File a Zakon o slobodnom pristupu informacijama request to CBCG for the current and prior-year procurement plans and the register of concluded contracts; in parallel search CEJN, which typically hosts contracting-authority plans, and check DRI audit reports which routinely quote plan figures.

coverage_gaps.description: How the RTS/X payment system and the TIPS Clone platform were actually contracted is unresolved. The TIPS Clone is World Bank financed (EUR 8m) and technically supplied via Banca d'Italia under Eurosystem auspices, which may mean much of it never passes through a competitive tender at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retrieve the World Bank project P509405 Procurement Plan and STEP contract awards, and check whether CBCG-Banca d'Italia cooperation is governed by a bilateral agreement published in Službeni list Crne Gore rather than a tender. Determine which components remain open to third-party vendors (connectivity, UX/marketing, security, integration).

coverage_gaps.description: Službeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette) was not queried in this pass. CBCG decisions, operating rules for the payment system, and international cooperation agreements are promulgated there.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add sluzbenilist.me to the source set and search for CBCG payment-system decisions and any agreement with Banca d'Italia, the ECB or the World Bank; these define the legal frame within which CBCG procures.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side sources were not scouted: banknote/coin processing and authentication suppliers (e.g. Giesecke+Devrient, Koenig & Bauer Banknote Solutions, Toshiba, Glory, CPS/cash-cycle integrators) and payments-platform integrators publish customer references, press releases and case studies that reveal CBCG contracts after award.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a vendor watchlist for cash-processing and payment-infrastructure suppliers active in the Western Balkans and monitor their news/reference pages for Montenegro mentions; the cma.se hit for 'Central Bank of Montenegro' seen in search results is an example of this vendor-case-study class and should be evaluated.

coverage_gaps.description: Searching was done in Montenegrin/Serbian Latin script only. Cyrillic-script variants ('Централна банка Црне Горе', 'јавне набавке') and Italian-language sources (Banca d'Italia's own TIPS Clone communications and procurement) were not queried.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries in Cyrillic transliteration and add Italian-language queries against bancaditalia.it for TIPS Clone partner-country arrangements and supplier selection.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth is thin. The CBCG tender page shows a sparse and uneven archive (2026, 2025, 2023, 2019, 2018) with apparent gaps, and no archived snapshots were checked.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Backfill from the Internet Archive (web.archive.org) for cbcg.me/me/javnost-rada/tenderi-i-oglasi across 2015-2026 to recover notices since removed, and cross-check against nabavke.com's CEJN document mirror.

brief: CBCG's procurement footprint is genuinely split across three channels, and only one of them is obvious. Its own site carries a live but sparse 'Tenderi i oglasi' page — the richest cell-specific find, currently listing instant-payments (TIPS Clone) connectivity, pre-implementation technical support and UX/marketing calls alongside jubilee-coin and construction notices — while offering no procurement plan, no contract register and no dedicated 'javne nabavke' section at all. The national CEJN portal is the statutory home for its domestic procedures but is a JavaScript application that yielded nothing to a plain fetch, so it is currently uncollectable without headless rendering. Most consequentially, the flagship purchases bypass both: the CBCG treasury and cash-processing equipment tender (banknote and coin processing, euro anti-counterfeiting, gold testing; deadline 7 October 2026) runs on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal under EC-ENEST references administered by the Ministry of Finance, and the TIPS Clone instant-payments build is financed by an EUR 8m World Bank loan and delivered via Banca d'Italia — meaning EU-portal, TED and World Bank project/STEP feeds are mandatory sources for this cell, and national-portal-only monitoring would miss almost everything that matters.
